lead: A log or stem is a naturally occurring block found in trees or huge fungi, primarily used as a building block and to create planks, a versatile crafting ingredient. There are currently ten types of logs: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, pale oak and poplar; and two types of stems: crimson and warped.
A stripped log or stripped stem is a variant of the log and stem, obtained by using an axe on a log or a stem respectively. Once stripped, it cannot be reversed.

Wood or hyphae is a block that has the log's "bark" texture on all six sides. It comes in 12 types: oak, spruce, birch, jungle, acacia, dark oak, mangrove, cherry, crimson, warped, pale oak, and poplar.
Stripped wood or stripped hyphae is a variant of wood obtained when any axe is used on wood or hyphae respectively.
A block of bamboo is a log-like block made of bamboo that can be used to craft bamboo planks.
A block of stripped bamboo is a variant of the block of bamboo made by using an axe on a block of bamboo.
A bamboo mosaic is a decorative block crafted out of bamboo slabs.

Planks are common blocks used as building blocks and in crafting recipes. They are usually one of the first things that a player crafts in Survival mode. There are currently 13 variants of planks, which can be differentiated into three categories: Overworld planks made from tree logs, bamboo planks made from blocks of bamboo, and nonflammable Nether planks made from huge fungus stems.
Stone is a block found underground in the Overworld or on the surface of mountains.
Cobblestone is a common block obtained from mining stone. It is mainly used for crafting or as a building block.
Mossy cobblestone is a variant of cobblestone with moss on it. It is mainly used for crafting or as a building block.
Smooth stone is a variant of stone made by smelting regular stone.
Stone bricks are a block found in various structures. It has three other variants: mossy stone bricks, cracked stone bricks, and chiseled stone bricks.
Chiseled stone bricks are a variant of stone bricks, crafted from stone brick slabs.
Cracked stone bricks are a variant of stone bricks, obtained through smelting and natural generation.
Mossy stone bricks are a variant of stone bricks.
Granite is a block of igneous rock, found in large pockets underground or in sulfur springs.
Polished granite is a processed and polished decorative form of granite.
Diorite is a block of igneous rock, found in large pockets underground.
Polished diorite is the polished version of diorite.
Andesite is a block of igneous rock, most often found in large pockets in the ground.
Polished andesite is the polished version of andesite.
Deepslate is a stone type found deep underground in the Overworld that functions similarly to regular stone, but takes significantly longer to mine.
Chiseled deepslate is a variant of deepslate. The block depicts a generic face not specific to any mob.
Cobbled deepslate is a stone variant that functions similar to cobblestone or blackstone.
Polished deepslate is the stone-like polished version of deepslate.
Deepslate bricks are the brick variant of deepslate.
Cracked deepslate bricks are the cracked variant of deepslate bricks.
Deepslate tiles are a decorative variant of deepslate.
Cracked deepslate tiles are the cracked variant of deepslate tiles.
Tuff is an ornamental rock, occurring in underground ore blobs below Y=0 and as part of sulfur springs.
Chiseled tuff is a chiseled variant of tuff.
Polished tuff is the polished version of tuff.
Tuff bricks are a brick variant of tuff found abundantly in trial chambers.
Chiseled tuff bricks are a variant of tuff bricks, featuring a large brick in the center of the block, with geometric designs above and below.
Bricks are a decorative building block.
Packed mud is a block crafted from mud and wheat. It is used to create mud bricks.
Mud bricks are a block obtained by crafting 4 packed mud.
Resin bricks are a block crafted from resin brick. It can also be crafted into its block family, containing slabs, stairs, walls, and the chiseled variant.
Chiseled resin bricks are a variant of resin bricks, crafted from resin brick slabs.

Sandstone is a solid block related to sand that comes in two color variants, the other being red sandstone. Regular sandstone is commonly found in deserts and beaches. Sandstone also has three decorative variants: chiseled sandstone, cut sandstone, and smooth sandstone.
Chiseled sandstone is a decorative variant of sandstone, crafted from sandstone slabs.
Cut sandstone is a variant of sandstone, obtained through crafting and stonecutting.
Smooth sandstone is a variant of sandstone, obtained by smelting sandstone.
Red sandstone is a variant of sandstone. It comes in three other variants: cut red sandstone, chiseled red sandstone, and smooth red sandstone.
Chiseled red sandstone is the chiseled variant of red sandstone, crafted from red sandstone slabs.
Cut red sandstone is a variant of red sandstone, obtained through crafting.
Smooth red sandstone is a variant of red sandstone, obtained by smelting.
Cinnabar is a decorative stone variant block that naturally generates in sulfur caves alongside sulfur, and as part of sulfur springs.
Chiseled cinnabar is a decorative chiseled variant of cinnabar used for building.
Polished cinnabar is the polished version of cinnabar.
Cinnabar bricks are a decorative brick variant of cinnabar.
Sulfur is a block that naturally generates in sulfur caves alongside cinnabar, in sulfur pools, and as part of sulfur springs.
Chiseled sulfur is a decorative chiseled variant of sulfur used for building.
Polished sulfur is a decorative polished variant of sulfur.
Sulfur bricks are a decorative brick variant of sulfur.
Prismarine is a type of stone that appears underwater in cold ocean ruins and ocean monuments. It periodically changes color between blue and green.
Prismarine bricks are a variant of prismarine, appearing as cyan bricks with chiseled patterns.
Dark prismarine is a variant of prismarine that has a dark cyan color with a tight grid pattern. It is one of the building blocks of ocean monuments along with other prismarine variants.

props.Flammable: No, but burns indefinitely on the top surface

lead: Netherrack is a frail stone block found abundantly in the Nether. Fire lit on top of netherrack burns indefinitely and cannot be extinguished by rain.
Nether bricks are the building blocks of Nether fortresses in the Nether and are used to spawn mobs in that structure.
Chiseled Nether bricks are a decorative variant of Nether bricks, crafted from Nether brick slabs.
Cracked Nether bricks are a decorative variant of Nether bricks, obtained by smelting Nether bricks.
Red Nether bricks are a decorative variant of Nether bricks that do not naturally generate.
Blackstone is a dark-colored block that functions similar to cobblestone or cobbled deepslate. It can only be found in the Nether.
Polished blackstone is the stone-like polished variation of blackstone.
Chiseled polished blackstone is the chiseled variation of polished blackstone. It has a piglin nose figure.
Polished blackstone bricks are a decorative version of polished blackstone.
Cracked polished blackstone bricks are the cracked variant of polished blackstone bricks.
Basalt is a block found in the basalt deltas in the Nether along with soul sand valleys and bastion remnants.
Polished basalt is the polished version of basalt and can be found as part of ancient cities and bastion remnants.
Smooth basalt is an ornamental rock smelted from basalt or found as part of amethyst geodes and ancient cities.
End stone is a block that appears in the End, and apart from generated structures, makes up all of the solid ground that exists in that dimension.
End stone bricks are decorative building blocks made of End stone that generate in End cities.
Purpur blocks are decorative blocks that can be crafted with popped chorus fruit and are naturally generated in End cities and End ships.
Purpur pillars are decorative blocks that can be crafted with purpur slabs and are naturally generated in End cities and End ships.

A block of quartz, internally known as a quartz block, is a mineral block used for decoration. It can be turned into a quartz slab, quartz stairs, chiseled quartz block, quartz pillar, quartz bricks, or smooth quartz block.
Quartz bricks are the brick variant of the block of quartz, obtained through crafting.
A chiseled quartz block is a variant of the block of quartz that can be crafted from quartz slabs.
A quartz pillar is a variant of the block of quartz, obtained through crafting.
A smooth quartz block is a mineral block used for decoration. It is made by smelting blocks of quartz.

A block of copper, internally known as a copper block, is a block that oxidizes over time, gaining a verdigris appearance over four stages. They can be prevented from oxidizing by being waxed with honeycombs. Non-oxidized blocks of copper are storage blocks equivalent to nine copper ingots.
Chiseled copper is a variant of copper blocks that generates in trial chambers.
Cut copper is an oxidizing metal block crafted from blocks of copper. Like other copper blocks, cut copper can be waxed to prevent oxidation.
Copper grates are a variant of copper blocks that have perforations that can be seen through.
A block of iron, known internally as an iron block, is a metal block equivalent to nine iron ingots.
A block of gold, internally known as a gold block, is a precious metal block equivalent to nine gold ingots.

A block of amethyst, known internally as an amethyst block, is a block found in amethyst geodes or crafted from amethyst shards. It can be placed next to a sculk sensor to "relay" received vibrations to other sculk sensors.
A block of coal, also known as a coal block, is a storage block, equivalent to nine coal, that can also be used as fuel.
A block of diamond, known internally as a diamond block, is a precious mineral block equivalent to nine diamonds.
A block of emerald, internally known as an emerald block, is a mineral block equivalent to nine emeralds.
A block of lapis lazuli, internally known as a lapis block, is a mineral block equivalent to nine pieces of lapis lazuli.

A block of netherite, internally known as a netherite block, is a precious metal block made from nine netherite ingots. In item form, it is immune to fire and lava, but can still be destroyed by a cactus.
A block of redstone, internally known as a redstone block, is a mineral block equivalent to nine redstone dust. It acts as an always active redstone power source that can be moved by pistons.

Crying obsidian is a luminous variant of obsidian that can be used to craft respawn anchors. Purple particles drip from its faces. Like obsidian, It has high hardness and blast resistance, making it immune to normal explosions. It can be obtained by mining it with a diamond or netherite pickaxe, and it cannot be crafted.
Gilded blackstone is a variant of blackstone found exclusively in bastion remnants, that can drop itself or gold nuggets when mined.

Reinforced deepslate is a block that generates exclusively in ancient cities. It has the highest hardness of any block, is immune to explosions, and cannot be pushed by pistons or obtained in Survival mode.
Bars are blocks that serve a similar purpose to glass panes, but made out of certain metal ingots instead of glass.
Iron bars are the iron variant of bars.
Copper bars are copper variants of bars. Unlike iron bars, they are colored copper orange and can oxidize over time, similar to other copper blocks.
A chain is a metallic decoration block made from ingots and nuggets.
Iron chains are metal decoration blocks and the iron variant of the chain.
A copper chain is an oxidizing directional block and the copper variant of chains.
A fence is a barrier block that cannot normally be jumped over, similar to a wall. Unlike a wall, a player (but not mobs) can see through the openings in a fence.
A wooden fence is the wooden variant of fences, crafted using planks and sticks.
A Nether brick fence is a Nether brick variant of fences used to form Nether fortresses in the Nether.
A slab is a half-height version of its respective block.

props.Transparent: Double slab: No Single slab: Partial (blocks light)‌[JE only]Partial (diffuses sky light)‌[BE only]

lead: A cut copper slab is a decorative slab variant of cut copper that generates in trial chambers and is used for building. Unlike other types of slabs, cut copper slabs can oxidize over time.

props.Transparent: Double slab: No Single slab: Partial (blocks light)‌[JE only]Partial (diffuses sky light)‌[BE only]

lead: A wooden slab is a wooden variant of a slab crafted from its respective planks.
Stairs are blocks that allow mobs and players to change elevation without jumping.
Cut copper stairs are a decorative stairs variant of cut copper that generate in trial chambers and are used for building. Unlike other types of stairs, cut copper stairs can oxidize over time.
Wooden stairs are a wooden variant of stairs, crafted from their respective planks.
A wall is a decorative block. Like fences, they can be used to create boundaries, because players and most mobs cannot climb or jump over them.
Wool is a block obtained from sheep that can be dyed in any of the sixteen different colors. It can be used as a crafting material and to block vibrations.

props.Transparent: Double slab: No Single slab: Partial (blocks light)‌[JE only]Partial (diffuses sky light)‌[BE only]

lead: A wool slab is a craftable slab variant of wool. It can be dyed in all 16 colors.
Wool stairs are a craftable stair variant of wool. They can be dyed in all 16 colors.
Carpets are thin variants of wool that can be dyed in any of the 16 colors.
Terracotta is a block that is found abundantly in badlands biomes, or can be obtained by smelting clay. It can be dyed to create stained terracotta.

Stained terracotta[note 1] is a dyed variant of terracotta obtained by crafting undyed terracotta with dyes. Some of the variants are found in badlands biomes, and all variants can be smelted into glazed terracotta.

Glazed terracotta is a vibrant solid block that comes in the sixteen regular dye colors, obtained by smelting stained terracotta. Glazed terracotta does not stick to slime blocks or honey blocks, and it cannot be pulled by sticky pistons, but it can be pushed by pistons.
Concrete is a block created when concrete powder touches water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.

props.Transparent: Double slab: No Single slab: Partial (blocks light)‌[JE only]Partial (diffuses sky light)‌[BE only]

lead: Concrete slabs are a craftable slab variant of concrete. They come in 16 colors.
Concrete stairs are a craftable stair variant of concrete. They come in 16 colors.
Concrete powder is a gravity-affected block that is converted to concrete when touching water. It comes in the sixteen dye colors.

Glass is a transparent solid block that can be dyed into stained glass, or crafted into tinted glass. It is also a versatile crafting ingredient used to craft harnesses, glass panes, beacons, daylight detectors, and End crystals.
A glass pane is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to glass blocks. It can be dyed into stained glass panes.
Tinted glass is a non-solid block that blocks light while being visually transparent.
Stained glass is a dyed variant of the glass block.
A stained glass pane is a dyed version of a glass pane. It is a transparent block that can be used as a more efficient alternative to stained glass blocks.

props.Luminous: Yes, when lit 1 candle: 3 2 candles: 6 3 candles: 9 4 candles: 12

lead: A candle is a dyable block that emits light when lit with a flint and steel. Up to four of the same color of candle can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced. Dyed candles are the dyed variants of candles that come in all sixteen colors. Once dyed, they cannot be changed into a different color.
An End rod is a decorative light source that emits white particles.
A froglight is a light-emitting block that is obtained when a frog eats a tiny magma cube. It comes in three variants based on the variant of frog that eats the magma cube.

Glowstone is a light-emitting block found hanging from ceilings and overhangs in the Nether. It can be used as a crafting material, broken into glowstone dust, and is required to fuel respawn anchors.
A jack o'lantern is a variant of pumpkin that emits light, and can be used to build golems.
A lantern is a block that emits light. It is brighter than a torch, and can be placed on top of or hang from the bottom of most blocks.
A copper lantern is a copper variant of a lantern that displays a green flame and oxidizes over time.
The soul lantern is a block that emits light. It is a variant of the lantern, and is crafted from a soul torch.

props.Transparent: Partial (suffocates mobs, blocks sunlight, blocks beacons)

lead: A sea lantern is an underwater light source that appears in ocean monuments and ocean ruins. It has an animated pulsing texture.
Torches are non-solid blocks that emit light.
A copper torch is a non-solid block that emits light. Copper torches can also be used to craft copper lanterns.
Soul torches are non-solid blocks that emit light. They are a variant of the torch crafted with the addition of soul soil or soul sand.
Colored torches are torches colored by metal chlorides, available in blue, red, purple, and green.
Elements and isotopes are blocks that are essential to chemistry in Bedrock Edition and Minecraft Education.

Hardened glass is a type of glass that has been chemically strengthened. Like normal glass, it is available in clear and colored variants, although the latter can only be obtained by dyeing regular stained glass beforehand.

A hardened glass pane is a type of block obtained by crafting with glass panes and several compounds. It also comes in 16 colors as stained variants, although a player must first dye regular glass panes into stained glass panes beforehand.
Hardened stained glass is the dyed type of hardened glass that has been chemically strengthened, crafted from stained glass.
A hardened stained glass pane is the dyed variant of hardened glass pane obtained by crafting with stained glass panes and several compounds.

Clay is a block that can be found abundantly in lush caves, in patches in shallow surface water or converted from mud using pointed dripstone. It can be smelted into terracotta or broken into clay balls which are smeltable into bricks.
Dirt is a block found abundantly in most biomes under a layer of grass blocks at the top of the Overworld as well as in patches underground.
Coarse dirt is a variant of dirt which grass blocks cannot spread to.

props.Transparent: JE: YesBE: Partial (allows light to pass through)

lead: Dirt paths are decorative blocks created by using a shovel on most types of dirt. They are mainly found in villages as a path for the villagers.
A grass block is a natural block that generates abundantly across the surface of the Overworld.
Mycelium is a particularly rare variant of dirt that is only found naturally in mushroom fields biomes. It has a particle effect that resembles tiny spores being released constantly from the surface.

Podzol is a dirt-type block that naturally blankets the surface of the old growth taiga and bamboo jungles, along with their respective variants. Grass blocks and mycelium cannot spread to this block.
Rooted dirt is a natural decorative block.
Gravel is a gravity-affected block found in the Overworld and the Nether. It is a source of flint, which has a chance to drop when gravel is broken.
Mud is a block found abundantly in mangrove swamps or created by using a water bottle on any type of dirt block. It can be used for crafting or converted into clay using pointed dripstone.
Crimson nylium is a variant of netherrack that generates in the Nether.
Warped nylium is a variant of netherrack that generates in the Nether.
Sand is a gravity-affected block found abundantly in deserts and beaches, and less commonly in or near surface water.
Red sand is a variant of sand found exclusively in badlands biomes. It can be used in place of sand in many crafting recipes, with the exception of concrete powder.

props.Flammable: No, but burns indefinitely on the top side as soul fire

lead: Soul sand is a block found primarily in the Nether that slows down entities walking on it unless they are wearing Soul Speed boots. It can also be used to grow Nether wart, create soul fire, make upward bubble columns, and spawn withers.

props.Flammable: No, but burns indefinitely when manually ignited on the top side only, creating soul fire

lead: Soul soil is a block found abundantly in soul sand valleys. It does not slow down entities, but still activates Soul Speed. It can also be used to create soul fire, and generate basalt when paired with blue ice and lava.
Bedrock is an indestructible block found in all three dimensions.

props.Flammable: No(burns indefinitely when manually ignited, top side only)

lead: A magma block is a light-emitting block found underwater in the Overworld, and commonly in the Nether. It deals burning damage while stood on, which can be prevented by sneaking. Underwater magma blocks produce bubble columns that pull entities downward and provide air.

Obsidian is a block found naturally in all dimensions. It is created when water flows over a lava source, or as part of structures. It has high hardness and blast resistance, making it immune to normal explosions. Obsidian can be used to craft beacons, enchanting tables, and ender chests, and build the frame of a Nether portal. Obsidian is only obtainable with a diamond or netherite pickaxe.
Calcite is a block exclusively found in geodes and stony peaks.

Sulfur spikes are blocks found in sulfur caves that form stalactites and stalagmites. Stalactites (which point downward) grow over time when attached from underneath sulfur and can serve as falling projectiles, similar to dripstone. Stalagmites (which point upward) do not deal extra fall damage, unlike pointed dripstone.

Potent sulfur is a block made from sulfur that produces noxious gas, which gives Nausea temporarily, if placed beneath shallow water. Placing a magma block below it in shallow water turns it into a geyser that occasionally erupts and launches entities upward. Placing lava below it causes a constant, non-stop eruption instead.

Pointed dripstone is a block found in dripstone caves that forms stalactites and stalagmites. Stalactites (which point downward) grow over time under certain conditions, can serve as falling projectiles, can renewably drip water and lava into cauldrons and convert mud into clay. Stalagmites (which point upward) deal extra damage to players and mobs that land on them.
Dripstone block is a rock block that allows pointed dripstone to grow beneath it if there is water on top of it.

Amethyst buds are the first three stages of growth of amethyst clusters, which grow on budding amethyst. Amethyst clusters are the fourth and final growth stage of amethyst buds, which drop amethyst shards when mined.

Amethyst buds are the first three stages of growth of amethyst clusters, which grow on budding amethyst. Amethyst clusters are the fourth and final growth stage of amethyst buds, which drop amethyst shards when mined.
Budding amethyst is a fragile block found in amethyst geodes that grows amethyst clusters over time. It drops nothing if it breaks, and cannot be moved from where it is found.

Ancient debris is a rare ore found in the Nether. It is the main source of netherite scraps, which can then be used to craft netherite ingots. Its high blast resistance makes it immune to normal explosions. In item form, it floats on lava and is completely immune to any form of fire.
Coal ore is a mineral block that drops coal when mined. Deepslate coal ore is a variant of coal ore that rarely generates at the top of the deepslate layer.
Coal ore is a mineral block that drops coal when mined. Deepslate coal ore is a variant of coal ore that rarely generates at the top of the deepslate layer.
Copper ore is an ore block found underground. Deepslate copper ore is the deepslate variant of copper ore, usually found deeper underground.
Copper ore is an ore block found underground. Deepslate copper ore is the deepslate variant of copper ore, usually found deeper underground.
A block of raw copper, internally known as a raw copper block, is a raw metal block equivalent to nine raw copper.

Diamond ore is a rare ore that generates deep underground, and drops diamonds when mined. Deepslate diamond ore is a variant of diamond ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs, and is more common than its regular variant.

Diamond ore is a rare ore that generates deep underground, and drops diamonds when mined. Deepslate diamond ore is a variant of diamond ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs, and is more common than its regular variant.

Emerald ore is a rare mineral block that generates only in mountains and windswept hills biomes. It drops emeralds when mined, or itself if mined with a pickaxe with the Silk Touch enchantment. Deepslate emerald ore is a rare variant of emerald ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs.

Emerald ore is a rare mineral block that generates only in mountains and windswept hills biomes. It drops emeralds when mined, or itself if mined with a pickaxe with the Silk Touch enchantment. Deepslate emerald ore is a rare variant of emerald ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs.
Gold ore is a rare mineral block found underground that drops raw gold when mined with an iron pickaxe or better. Deepslate gold ore is a variant of gold ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff.
Gold ore is a rare mineral block found underground that drops raw gold when mined with an iron pickaxe or better. Deepslate gold ore is a variant of gold ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff.
Nether gold ore is a type of gold ore found in the Nether that drops gold nuggets instead of raw gold when broken. As with other gold blocks, breaking Nether gold ore will anger nearby piglins.
A block of raw gold, internally known as a raw gold block, is a raw metal block equivalent to nine raw gold.

Iron ore is a mineral block typically found underground. It is a source of raw iron, which can be smelted into iron ingots. Deepslate iron ore is the deepslate variant of iron ore. It is found in deepslate layers.

Iron ore is a mineral block typically found underground. It is a source of raw iron, which can be smelted into iron ingots. Deepslate iron ore is the deepslate variant of iron ore. It is found in deepslate layers.
A block of raw iron, known internally as a raw iron block, is a raw metal block equivalent to nine raw iron.

props.Hardness: Lapis Lazuli Ore: 3 Deepslate Lapis Lazuli Ore: 4.5

lead: Lapis lazuli ore, internally known as lapis ore, is the ore block from which lapis lazuli is obtained. Deepslate lapis lazuli ore, internally known as deepslate lapis ore, is a variant of lapis lazuli ore that generates in deepslate layers.

props.Hardness: Lapis Lazuli Ore: 3 Deepslate Lapis Lazuli Ore: 4.5

lead: Lapis lazuli ore, internally known as lapis ore, is the ore block from which lapis lazuli is obtained. Deepslate lapis lazuli ore, internally known as deepslate lapis ore, is a variant of lapis lazuli ore that generates in deepslate layers.
Nether quartz ore is an ore found in the Nether, and is a source of quartz.
Redstone ore is the ore block from which redstone dust is obtained. Deepslate redstone ore is a variant of redstone ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs.
Redstone ore is the ore block from which redstone dust is obtained. Deepslate redstone ore is a variant of redstone ore that can generate in deepslate and tuff blobs.
An azalea is a solid block that can be grown into an azalea tree.
A flowering azalea is a variant of azalea that counts as a flower for all purposes, including pollination by bees, except for crafting dyes.

Bamboo is a versatile, fast-growing plant found primarily in jungles, used for crafting (particularly scaffolding and bamboo wood), smelting, and breeding pandas. A bamboo shoot is the initial non-solid sapling form of planted bamboo.

A big dripleaf is a plant that generates within lush caves. Its leaf is a temporary platform; when stood on, it tilts down and drops its burden, resetting a few seconds later. The leaf can be powered to prevent it from tilting.
A small dripleaf is a plant which generates in lush caves, and is used to grow big dripleaves, a platforming block.
A bush is a non-solid plant block found in many grassy biomes. Its color is biome-dependent, and matches the color of grass blocks.
A cactus is a plant block found in deserts and badlands. It grows over time and can sprout cactus flowers. It damages mobs and destroys minecarts and dropped items that touch it.

A creaking heart is a living block that can be crafted or found in pale oak trees in pale gardens. It activates if placed in a line between two pale oak logs; then, during nighttime, it spawns a creaking and protects it from all damage. Breaking a creaking heart that is protecting a creaking instantly kills it. Hitting a protected creaking causes resin clumps to grow on pale oak logs near its link
A dead bush is a non-solid plant block found in deserts, badlands, swamps, and old growth taigas. It can only be obtained with shears, and otherwise drops sticks when broken.
Ferns are non-solid plant blocks found only in certain biomes and have the same characteristics as grass.
A large fern is a 2-block tall variant of the fern.
A firefly bush is a decorative plant that produces firefly particles around it when exposed to darkness.
Hanging roots are a natural decorative block found underground in the lush caves biome.
Leaf litter is a thin decorative block resembling fallen leaves. Up to four can be placed in the same block space.

Leaves are transparent blocks that generate as part of trees and are sources of their respective saplings. They dissipate over time when not attached to logs, but persist when placed by players. Falling leaf particles occasionally drop from leaves.
Oak leaves are biome-colored leaves that form the canopy of oak trees and jungle bushes, and can drop apples.
Spruce leaves are evergreen leaves that form the canopy of spruce trees.
Birch leaves are evergreen leaves that form the canopy of birch trees.
Jungle leaves are biome-colored leaves that form the canopy of jungle trees. Their sapling drop rate is twice as rare as any other leaves.
Acacia leaves are biome-colored leaves that form the canopy of acacia trees.
Dark oak leaves are biome-colored leaves that form the canopy of dark oak trees, and can drop apples.
Mangrove leaves are biome-colored leaves that form the canopy of mangrove trees. They can grow mangrove propagules by applying bone meal.
Cherry leaves are leaves that form the canopy of cherry trees and function as flowers for bee mechanics. They are colored pink which does not change with the biome they are placed in.
Pale oak leaves are leaves that form the canopy of pale oak trees. They are colored gray which does not change with the biome they are placed in.
Azalea leaves are evergreen leaves that generate as part of azalea trees and drop azaleas. Flowering azalea leaves are a variant that function as flowers for bee mechanics and drop flowering azaleas.
Poplar leaves are leaves that form the canopy of poplar trees with yellow, orange, and red color variants that do not change with the biome.

A mangrove propagule is an amphibious sapling that can grow into a mangrove tree. They grow hanging from mangrove leaves when the leaves are bone mealed or when a tree is first created, but can only be obtained as items if fully grown.
Mangrove roots are blocks that form as part of mangrove trees. Unlike other see-through blocks such as copper grates, mangrove roots are capable of conducting redstone power.
Muddy mangrove roots are a decorative variant of mangrove roots with dirt-like properties.
A moss block is a natural block that can be spread to other blocks by using bone meal.
A moss carpet is a thin decorative variant of the moss block, resembling a carpet in functionality.
A pale moss block is a block that generates in pale gardens. Unlike regular moss blocks, pale moss blocks are flammable.
A pale moss carpet is a block that causes vine-like pale moss to grow on the side of neighboring blocks.
Pale hanging moss is a block found under the logs and leaves of pale oaks. When attached to a pale oak log or leaves, it emits ambient sounds.
A red shrub is a non-solid plant block found in dappled forests. Red shrubs are not biome tinted like most other plants, keeping their red color regardless of the biome they are placed in.

A resin clump is a block generated by a creaking heart on pale oaks in any biome when a creaking is attacked. It also drops when a creaking heart is mined or destroyed. It can be used to craft decorative blocks of resin, and can also be smelted to produce resin bricks, which in turn can be crafted into the whole resin brick block family.

A block of resin, internally known as a resin block, is a block equivalent to nine resin clumps. It acts as a good temporary block being broken instantly without having any special properties, and can be used to craft creaking hearts.
A sapling is a non-solid block that can be grown into a tree.
Short dry grass is a one-block tall foliage block that generates frequently in deserts and all types of badlands. It grows on sand and terracotta. It can also be eaten by sheep.

Tall dry grass is the tall variant of dry grass. Unlike other tall variants of foliage, this block is only one-block tall. It generates frequently in deserts and all types of badlands, and looks like a more full version of short dry grass. It also grows on sand and terracotta, and can be eaten by sheep.
Short grass is a non-solid plant block that may drop wheat seeds when broken. Its color is biome-dependent, and matches the color of grass blocks.
Tall grass is the 2-block tall variant of short grass.
Vines are climbable non-solid vegetation blocks that grow on walls.
An allium is a flower that can be crafted into magenta dye and suspicious stew.
An azure bluet is a flower that can be crafted into light gray dye and suspicious stew.
A blue orchid is a flower that generates exclusively in swamp biomes. It is used to craft light blue dye and suspicious stew.
A cactus flower is a type of flower that grows from cacti. It can be placed on any solid top surface or crafted into pink dye.
A cornflower is a flower that can be crafted into blue dye and suspicious stew.
A dandelion is a flower that can be crafted into yellow dye, suspicious stew, and golden dandelions, and can be used to breed and lure rabbits.

A golden dandelion is a craftable flower that can be fed to baby mobs to pause their aging, or resume it by feeding another one to the same baby mob. It does not generate naturally and can only be obtained through crafting or the wandering trader.

An eyeblossom is a unique flower found in the pale garden biome. It changes state depending on the daylight cycle, closing during the day and opening at night. Its "eye", visible only when the flower is open, glows in the dark but does not emit light in its surroundings.

An eyeblossom is a unique flower found in the pale garden biome. It changes state depending on the daylight cycle, closing during the day and opening at night. Its "eye", visible only when the flower is open, glows in the dark but does not emit light in its surroundings.

An eyeblossom is a unique flower found in the pale garden biome. It changes state depending on the daylight cycle, closing during the day and opening at night. Its "eye", visible only when the flower is open, glows in the dark but does not emit light in its surroundings.
A lilac is a tall flower that can be crafted into magenta dye.
A lily of the valley is a flower often found in forested biomes that can be crafted into white dye and suspicious stew.
An oxeye daisy[a] is a flower that can be crafted into light gray dye, suspicious stew, and flower charge banner patterns.
A peony is a tall flower that can be crafted into pink dye.
Pink petals are a decorative block that generates in cherry grove biomes.
A pitcher plant is a tall ancient flower that grows from a pitcher pod.
A pitcher pod is an ancient bulbous seed that has a chance to be dropped by sniffers when they finish digging. It is the seed of pitcher plants.
A poppy is a red flower that can be crafted into red dye and suspicious stew with the Night Vision effect.
A rose bush is a tall flower that can be crafted into red dye.
A spore blossom is a ceiling-hanging decorative block that generates in lush caves and emits green particles.
A sunflower is a tall flower that generates exclusively in sunflower plains biomes. It can be crafted into two yellow dye.
A torchflower is an ancient flower obtained from harvesting torchflower seeds. It can be crafted into orange dye.
Torchflower seeds are ancient seeds that have a chance to be dropped by sniffers when they finish digging. It is the seed of torchflowers.

Tulips are a kind of flower found in plains and flower forests that come in multiple colored variants: red, orange, white, and pink. They yield dyes of their respective colors, with the exception of white tulips, which yield light gray dye, and all of them are used to craft suspicious stew.
Wildflowers are a thin decorative flower that can be placed four times in the space of one block, similar to pink petals and leaf litter.
A wither rose is a flower that inflicts the Wither effect on players and mobs that touch it. It drops when a mob or player is killed by a wither.
Beetroot seeds[a] are items that can be used to plant beetroot crops. Beetroot crops are planted in farmland and used to grow beetroot and beetroot seeds.
Carrots are a food item obtained from carrot crops that can be consumed, used to plant carrot crops, or used as a crafting ingredient. Carrot crops are planted in farmland and used to grow carrots.

Glow berries are a food item obtained from cave vines and can be used to plant them. Cave vines are a climbable plant that hangs off ceilings and grows glow berries. Cave vines with glow berries produce light.
Chorus plants are blocks that naturally generate on the outer islands of the End. They drop chorus fruit when broken. They can also be grown using chorus flowers.

Chorus flowers are plant blocks harvested from chorus plants, and can be placed on End stone to grow more chorus plants. A chorus flower will only drop as an item if broken directly or shot with a projectile.

Cocoa beans are items obtained from cocoa pods, and are used to plant more of them as well as to craft brown dye and cookies. Cocoa pods are plant blocks that can only be placed on jungle log sides and grow cocoa beans. They can be found naturally in jungles.
A melon[a] is a fruit block that grows from a fully-grown melon stem, which in turn is grown from melon seeds.

Melon seeds[a] are items obtained from melon slices that can be used to grow melon stems. Melon stems are plants grown on farmland that, over time, grow melons on dirt, mud and moss blocks adjacent to them.

A potato is a food item obtained from potato crops that can be used to plant them, consumed raw or cooked to make baked potatoes. Potato crops are planted in farmland and used to grow potatoes and, rarely, poisonous potatoes.
A pumpkin is a block found in patches in grassy biomes or grown from pumpkin seeds, which it can also be crafted into. Using shears on a pumpkin carves a face into it and drops pumpkin seeds.
A carved pumpkin is a block obtained by using shears on a pumpkin. It is used to craft jack o'lanterns, build golems, and can be worn as a helmet.

Pumpkin seeds are items obtained from pumpkins that can be used to grow pumpkin stems. Pumpkin stems are plants grown on farmland that, over time, grow pumpkins on dirt, mud, and moss blocks adjacent to them.

Sugar cane is a plant that can only be placed on plantable blocks adjacent to water. It grows up to three blocks tall over time, but will instead uproot itself if its water is removed. Sugar cane can be crafted into sugar and paper.

Sweet berries are a food item obtained from sweet berry bushes and are used to plant them. Sweet berry bushes are quick-growing plants that grow sweet berries. Players and most mobs are slowed down and take constant damage while moving through them. They can be found naturally in taigas and snowy taigas.

Wheat seeds are items obtained by breaking grass, or more abundantly harvested from wheat crops, and are used to plant them. Wheat crops are planted in farmland and used to grow wheat and wheat seeds.

Hay bales[a] are storage blocks equivalent to nine pieces of wheat. They are used as a crafting ingredient, to feed llamas and all living horse variants, reduce fall damage, and extend campfire smoke.

A brown mushroom is a fungus found in the Overworld and the Nether. It can only be planted in mycelium, nylium, podzol, or darkness, which also allows it to spread over time or receive bone meal to grow into a huge brown mushroom.

A red mushroom is a fungus found in the Overworld and the Nether. It can only be planted on mycelium, nylium, podzol, or in darkness, which also allows it to spread over time or receive bone meal to grow into a huge red mushroom.
A shelf mushroom is a fungus that grows on poplar trees. It has two sizes and causes entities to bounce when they fall on it.
A mushroom block is a solid block that makes up a huge mushroom, which consists of a mushroom stem and brown mushroom blocks or red mushroom blocks, depending on the color of the huge mushroom.
A glow lichen is a non-solid, light-emitting block. It can generate, or be placed, on any side of a solid block. It primarily generates on the side of blocks in caves.

A crimson fungus is a fungus found in crimson and warped forests or by using bone meal on nylium. It can grow into a huge crimson fungus if bone mealed, but only if planted on crimson nylium. It can also be fed to hoglins.

A warped fungus is a fungus found in warped and crimson forests or by using bone meal on nylium. It can grow into a huge warped fungus if bone mealed, but only if planted on warped nylium. It can also be used for crafting, fed to striders or be planted to repel hoglins.

Nether wart is a fungus harvested from Nether wart crops and is used to plant them. It is an essential ingredient in almost every potion. Unlike other crimson plants, Nether wart doesn't have a warped equivalent, although warped wart blocks exist. Nether wart crops are found in Nether fortresses and bastion remnants and used to grow Nether wart, which only requires soul sand to grow.
Nether sprouts are a non-solid fungi block that generate in warped forests. Unlike other warped forest plants, it does not have a crimson equivalent.
Crimson roots are a non-solid "plant" block that generate naturally on nylium and soul soil in few Nether biomes. They resemble a colony of tall, thin mushrooms.
Warped roots are a non-solid "plant" block which generate naturally on warped nylium and soul soil in warped forests. They resemble a colony of tall, thin mushrooms.
Nether wart blocks are decorative blocks found in crimson forests and crafted using Nether wart.
Warped wart blocks are a decorative block found in warped forests, generating as part of huge warped fungus.
Shroomlights are light-emitting blocks that generate in huge fungi.
Twisting vines are climbable upward-growing vegetation blocks found in the Nether in warped forests.
Weeping vines are climbable, downwards-growing vegetation blocks found in the Nether in crimson forests.

props.Stackable: Yes (64) without bees insideNo with bee(s) inside

lead: Bee nests are blocks found attached to certain trees. They house bees, which fill their homes with honey made from gathered flower nectar. Full bee nests can be harvested for honeycombs (using shears) or honey bottles (using glass bottles). Bees attack players who harvest or break their homes without utilizing campfires or Silk Touch, respectively.
Honeycomb blocks are decorative blocks crafted from honeycombs.
Bone blocks are storage blocks equivalent to 9 pieces of bone meal.
A cobweb is a block that drastically slows down the movement of most entities touching it. The Weaving effect lessens this movement speed decrease.

The dragon egg is a gravity-affected block that can be obtained only once per world (or twice in Bedrock Edition) by defeating the ender dragon. It teleports to avoid being mined, but drops as an item if it falls onto a non-full block such as a torch or is pushed by a piston.

A dried ghast is an immobile, shriveled, harmless ghast in the form of a block. It can be found near Nether fossils, obtained through bartering, or crafted. Placing it in water causes it to hydrate over time until it becomes a ghastling.

props.Renewable: Deepslate variant: No All others: Yes
props.Hardness: Stone and stone bricks: 0.75 Cobblestone: 1 Deepslate: 1.5

lead: An infested block is a stone, stone variant or deepslate block inhabited by a silverfish, which can break out if it is mined or a nearby silverfish is attacked. Infested blocks break more quickly, do not drop as items and can be safely cleaned of infestation using Silk Touch.
A sniffer egg is a block that can be brushed out of suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins, or obtained by breeding two sniffers. It slowly hatches into a snifflet (baby sniffer) when placed.
A turtle egg is a block that can be placed up to four times within one block space that hatches turtles.
Coral is a type of non-solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn. Each of them are vibrant and colorful, but turn gray when they die.
A dead coral is the dead variant of coral. There are five variants total: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
A coral block is a solid block that comes in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
A dead coral block is a dead variant of a coral block. These blocks are always gray. There are five variants total: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
Coral fans are non-solid blocks that come in five variants: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
Dead coral fans are the result of the living variants of coral fans when they are outside water. There are five variants total: tube, brain, bubble, fire, and horn.
Frogspawn is a non-solid block laid by frogs when they are bred, which hatches into tadpoles over time. It cannot be obtained as an item or moved by a piston.

Kelp is aquatic algae found in all oceans except for warm oceans, frozen oceans, and deep frozen oceans. It can be planted underwater and grows over time (though not forever) or from bone meal usage. Smelting it results in dried kelp, which is edible and craftable into dried kelp blocks.
Dried kelp blocks are storage blocks equivalent to nine dried kelp. They can also be used as fuel.
A lily pad is a plant block found in swamps, mangrove swamps, and as fishing loot. It can only be placed on water or waterlogged blocks and can be stood on as a platform.

props.Luminous: Yes, when waterlogged 1 sea pickle: 6 2 sea pickles: 9 3 sea pickles: 12 4 sea pickles: 15

lead: A sea pickle is a block found in warm oceans. While in water it emits light, and can be spread using bone meal if placed on a living coral block. Up to four sea pickles can be placed in one block space, which affects the amount of light produced while in water.
Seagrass is a non-solid plant block that generates underwater in most aquatic biomes. Tall seagrass is a two-block high variety of seagrass.
Sculk is a block found abundantly in the deep dark or converted from other blocks by a sculk catalyst. Like most of the rest of the sculk family, it drops experience when broken by a tool.
A sculk catalyst is a sculk block that "blooms" when a mob or player dies nearby, which may convert nearby blocks to sculk blocks (except for other sculk catalysts).

A sculk sensor is a sculk block that detects vibrations caused by nearby actions and events and emits a redstone signal in response. Player-caused vibrations can also trigger nearby sculk shriekers. Sneaking prevents the creation of vibrations while moving, and wool can be used to block or prevent them. Placing an amethyst block next to a sculk sensor allows it to "relay" detected vibrations to ot

A calibrated sculk sensor is a craftable type of sculk sensor that functions similarly, but detects vibrations more quickly and from further away. Its amethyst-covered input side can be powered to make the sensor only detect vibrations from specific sources, depending on the signal strength used. Placing an amethyst block next to a calibrated sculk sensor allows it to "relay" detected vibrations t

A sculk shrieker is a sculk block that "shrieks" if any player touches its top (even indirectly) or activates a nearby sculk sensor. Only players can trigger it. Naturally-generated sculk shriekers appear only in the deep dark biome. They also inflict Darkness and may summon a warden if triggered, but shriekers placed by players or sculk catalysts are completely inert and harmless.
A sculk vein is a block found in the deep dark or generated by sculk catalysts. It can generate or be placed on any side of a solid block.
Lava is a light-emitting fluid that causes fire damage, mostly found in the lower reaches of the Overworld and the Nether.

props.Transparent: JE: Partial (diffuses sky light)BE: Partial (diffuses sky light, -1 to light)

lead: Water is a fluid that naturally generates abundantly in the Overworld.

A bubble column is an air-providing vertical water current. It is created by magma blocks and soul sand and, depending on the block used, will either pull entities downward or push them upward, respectively.

props.Transparent: JE: Partial (-1 to light)BE: Partial (diffuses sky light, -2 to light)

lead: Ice is a transparent block formed from frozen water, which it can melt into if broken or exposed to bright light. Its top face is slippery for most entities and causes ridden boats to move at high speeds.

Blue ice is a solid block similar to packed ice and ice, but much more slippery. It is the fastest ice type for boat riding and can be used to generate basalt in conjunction with soul soil and lava. It does not melt when placed near light sources.
Packed ice[a] is a variant of ice that functions almost identically, but does not melt and is opaque instead of transparent. Like other types of ice, it can only be obtained using a Silk Touch tool.
Ice crystals are an upcoming light-emitting block that generate in the ice caves, announced in Minecraft Live - September 2026. They are expected to function similarly to amethyst buds.

An icicle is a block which generates in ice caves. They form stalactites, and will melt and subsequently fall if there is enough light nearby. They only naturally generate on ceilings, but can also be placed on floors.
Snow is a ground cover and gravity-affected‌[Bedrock Edition only] block found on the surface in snowy biomes. It can be replenished during snowfall.

Powder snow is a non-solid block found in snowy slopes and groves, or collected from snowfall using cauldrons. It slows down and deals freezing damage to most entities within it. Wearing any leather armor prevents freezing, while wearing leather boots allow powder snow to be walked on and climbed through. It can only be obtained using a bucket and melts when placed inside water.
A snow block is a full-sized block of snow.

Air is an invisible block used to define unoccupied space where other blocks and items could exist; it represents the absence of a block or an item. It is one of the few blocks in the game that players cannot normally interact with. Cave air‌[Java Edition only] is a variant found only underground in carver caves[verify for Java Edition] and some generated structures along with features like lava l
Invisible bedrock is an invisible block used to create a world boundary around Old worlds and the void floor in Bedrock Edition.
Fire is a non-solid block that can spread to nearby flammable blocks and destroy them.
Soul fire is a dimmer turquoise variation of fire that is created when soul sand or soul soil is ignited. Soul fire deals more damage than normal fire and does not spread.

props.Transparent: JE: YesBE: Partial (diffuses sky light, -2 to light)

lead: An anvil is a gravity-affected utility block used to rename items, combine enchantments and repair items without losing the enchantments. An anvil has limited durability, and as it is used or dropped too far, gradually becomes a chipped anvil, then a damaged anvil, then breaks and disappears, without dropping anything in return.
A barrel is a solid block used to store items. Unlike a chest, it cannot connect to other barrels. It also serves as a fisherman's job site block.

A beacon is a block that can be placed in view of the sky, on top of a pyramid made of valuable mineral blocks, to activate it. Once active, it projects a beam upward and can be set to provide constant status effects to all players in a radius around it. A beacon's range and available effects depend on the size of its pyramid base, between one and four layers.

props.Transparent: JE: YesBE: Partial (diffuses sky light, -2 to light)

lead: A brewing stand is a block used for brewing potions using water bottles and suitable ingredients. It also serves as a cleric's job site block.
A cartography table is a utility block used for cloning, zooming out, and locking maps. It also serves as a cartographer's job site block.
A chest is a block used to store items. A large chest (or "double chest") is the combination of two adjacent chests, and can store twice as many items.
An ender chest is a type of chest whose contents are exclusive to each player, and they can be placed and accessed from anywhere in any dimension.

A copper chest is a type of chest made of copper. It functions almost identically to a normal wooden chest, except that it oxidizes over time, and copper golems remove items from it to store inside nearby wooden chests. Like normal chests, two copper chests can merge into a large copper chest if placed adjacent each other.
A crafting table is a utility block that gives access to all crafting recipes, including many not available from the inventory's crafting grid.

An enchanting table is a block used to spend experience and lapis lazuli to apply enchantments to tools, armor and books. Surrounding it with up to fifteen bookshelves increases both its enchanting power and level requirement.
A furnace is a block with two functions: it can be used for either smelting or cooking, by placing fuel and an appropriate item inside together.
A blast furnace is a block that smelts ores and metal items twice as quickly as a furnace, but cannot smelt anything else. It also serves as an armorer's job site block.
A smoker is a block that cooks food twice as quickly as a furnace, but cannot smelt anything else. It also serves as a butcher's job site block.

A grindstone is a block used to remove all enchantments, except for curses, from items, refunding some experience orbs. Additionally, it can repair tools, weapons, and armor. It also serves as a weaponsmith's job site block.
A lectern is a block used to display a book and quill or written book for reading. Turning a page triggers a redstone pulse. It also serves as a librarian's job site block.
A loom is a block used to apply customizable and layerable designs to banners using dyes. Some designs require banner patterns to apply. It also serves as a shepherd's job site block.
A shulker box is a dyeable block that stores items, and, unlike all other storage blocks, keeps its contents in item form when broken.

props.Catches firefrom lava: JE: Yes, except Crimson and Warped SignsBE: Yes

lead: A sign is a non-solid block that can display text, and can be placed on the top or side of other blocks. The text of signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent its text from being edited by any player.

A hanging sign is a variant of a sign that displays text, and can be placed underneath blocks or with a solid self-supporting bracket. The text of hanging signs can be customized with dyes and glow ink sacs, and they can be waxed to prevent edits.
A smithing table is a utility block used to apply smithing templates to tools, weapons, and armor. It also serves as a toolsmith's job site block.
A stonecutter is a block used to easily craft many stone and copper blocks, and is cheaper than normal crafting for stairs and copper variants. It is also a job site block for mason villagers.

A banner is a block that can be crafted in 16 different colors, customized in a loom using dyes and banner patterns, and applied to a shield. In Java Edition, banners can also be used to add markers to maps.
An ominous banner is a special uncraftable variant of the banner obtained from raid captains and pillager outposts.

lead: Beehives are craftable blocks that house bees, which fill their homes with honey made from gathered flower nectar. Full beehives can be harvested for honeycombs (using shears) or honey bottles (using glass bottles). Bees attack players who harvest or break their homes without utilizing campfires or Silk Touch, respectively.

A bed is a dyeable utility block that allows a player in the Overworld to sleep through the night and change their spawn point to within a few blocks of the bed, as long as it is not broken or obstructed. Villagers sleep in beds at night and require spare beds to produce offspring.

props.Flammable: JE: Drops when hit with fireBE: Yes

lead: A straw bed is a single-use utility block that allows a player in the Overworld to sleep through the night without resetting their spawn point. It breaks without dropping anything when the player wakes up in the morning or leaves the bed mid-sleep.

A bell is a block that can be rung by hand, with a projectile or using a redstone signal to make all nearby villagers run to their beds. In Java Edition, this also reveals all illager-related mobs in a large radius. It can be found in villages or purchased from villagers, and cannot be crafted.
A bookshelf is a block that improves enchantments applied with an enchanting table when placed around one, up to a maximum of fifteen bookshelves, at the expense of level requirement.

lead: A cake is a block that can serve as food. It can be eaten by placing and using it, with each use consuming one of its seven slices. The entire cake gives the most hunger points out of every food item, but has low saturation. A cake with candle is an uneaten cake with any type of candle placed on it, which can be lit with a flint and steel to emit light.
A campfire is a block that can be used to cook food, pacify bees, or act as a spread-proof light source, a smoke signal, or a damaging trap.

Soul campfires are dimmer variants of campfires. Soul campfires deal more damage than normal campfires and have turquoise flames. Just like normal campfires, they can be used to cook food, pacify bees, or act as a spread-proof light source, smoke signal, or damaging trap block. Crafting soul campfires with soul sand and then breaking them to convert the soul sand into soul soil (similarly to conve

lead: A cauldron is a block that can contain water, lava, or powder snow and, in certain situations, collect them from the environment. In Bedrock Edition, it can also hold dyed water or potions and can be used to efficiently create tipped arrows. It also serves as a leatherworker's job site block.
Chiseled bookshelves are blocks that can hold books, books and quills, written books, enchanted books, and knowledge books.
sections: Hoppers, minecarts with hoppers, and droppers

lead: A composter is a block that converts some biological material into bone meal. It also serves as a farmer's job site block.

A conduit is a block that can be placed underwater and surrounded by prismarine to activate it. Once active, it empowers nearby players touching water or rain, prevents them from drowning, and attacks wet monsters.

A copper golem statue is the result of a copper golem fully oxidizing and petrifying into a block. It can be posed in four different ways, or it can be reanimated by scraping it with an axe enough times.

props.Renewable: Only bricks: YesWith pottery sherd(s): No

lead: A decorated pot is a storage block crafted from bricks and/or pottery sherds, with the items used individually affecting the appearance of its four side faces. It can store a single inventory slot's worth of items, which cannot be seen or retrieved by hand without breaking the pot.

The End gateway is a block that forms a part of End gateways, which teleport the player between the central island and the outer islands in the End. It is one of two blocks that use the starfield effect.

The End portal block is a block generated when an End portal or exit portal is activated, which teleports the player between the Overworld and the End. It is one of two blocks that use the starfield effect.

An End portal frame is an indestructible block, 12 of which form an End portal. Eyes of ender must be inserted into all 12 empty frames (if not already present upon generation) for the portal to activate and allow passage into the End dimension.

props.Transparent: Java Edition: Partial (Blocks light)Bedrock Edition: Yes

lead: Farmland is a block created by using a hoe on most types of dirt, and is required to grow seeds, carrots, and potatoes. Water and rain can hydrate farmland, improving crop growth. It reverts to dirt if broken, landed on repeatedly or left dehydrated and unplanted long enough.
The fletching table is a fletcher's job site block that can generate naturally in villages. It is used to turn an unemployed villager into a fletcher.
A flower pot is a decorative block that can contain flowers, bamboo, saplings, cacti, mushrooms, fungi, and other small plants.

props.Transparent: JE: Partial (-1 to light)BE: Partial (diffuses sky light, -2 to light)

lead: Frosted ice is a translucent block created when a mob or entity wearing Frost Walker-enchanted boots moves over water. It cannot be obtained as an item and will quickly crack and melt if exposed to light or sunlight.
Heads (including skulls) are a group of 7 blocks based on the heads of players and 6 different mobs. All heads can be worn as helmets and serve as special note block instruments.
A skeleton skull is the head of a skeleton in the form of a block. It can be obtained from ancient cities or by killing a skeleton using a charged creeper's explosion.

A wither skeleton skull is the head of a wither skeleton in the form of a block, which is a rare drop from killed wither skeletons. Three of them can be used to summon a wither, a destructive boss mob that is the only source of Nether stars.
A zombie head is the head of a zombie in the form of a block. It can only be obtained by killing a zombie using a charged creeper's explosion.
A creeper head is the head of a creeper in the form of a block. It can only be obtained by killing a creeper using a different charged creeper's explosion.
A piglin head is the head of a piglin in the form of a block. It can only be obtained by killing a piglin using a charged creeper's explosion.
A dragon head[a] is a block that resembles a smaller version of the ender dragon's head. It can only be obtained from End ships.
A heavy core is a rare block that can only be obtained from ominous vaults found in trial chambers. It can be combined with a breeze rod to craft a mace.
A jukebox is a block used to insert and play music discs. Playing a disc causes it to produce a redstone signal and allows nearby allays to duplicate when given amethyst shards.
The ladder is a block used for climbing vertically or horizontally. They can be placed only on the sides of other blocks.
A lodestone is a block that can be used to alter compasses to point toward it.

A monster spawner is a type of spawner found in a variety of structures. It constantly summons instances of the mob displayed within it as long as a player is in range and the light levels are correct for that mob type to spawn nearby. It only drops experience orbs when broken, and cannot be moved from where it is found.
The Nether portal block is the translucent part of the Nether portal that teleports the player to and from the Nether.
The respawn anchor is a block that allows the player to set their spawn point in the Nether, provided it's fueled with glowstone blocks.

Scaffolding is a climbable semi-solid block with a stable top platform and unique placement controls that simplify creating columns and bridges. Scaffolding pieces fall downward if placed too far away from a supporting block, which can naturally form into more supporting columns.

A shelf is a block that can store and display up to three stacks of items. Using an item slot exchanges its contents with the player's hotbar. Powering a shelf combines its three slots together and makes using it swap everything at once. Two or three adjacent shelves can merge their slots together if all are powered, which allows for swapping six or nine items at a time, respectively.

A sponge is a block that can be placed to remove water in an area around itself. This turns it into a wet sponge, which can be smelted or placed in the Nether to dry it to be reused. Sponges can only be found in ocean monuments.

A sponge is a block that can be placed to remove water in an area around itself. This turns it into a wet sponge, which can be smelted or placed in the Nether to dry it to be reused. Sponges can only be found in ocean monuments.

Suspicious gravel is a fragile gravity-affected block found in various Overworld structures. It can be brushed to extract unique structure-dependent loot from it. It drops nothing if it breaks, and breaks if it falls or is moved.

Suspicious sand is a fragile gravity-affected block found in various Overworld structures. It can be brushed to extract unique structure-dependent loot from it. It drops nothing if it breaks, and will break if it falls or is moved.

TNT is an explosive block that can be lit by a redstone signal, flint and steel, stray fire, flaming projectile or explosion. When lit, TNT becomes primed TNT, a gravity-affected entity that produces a damaging, block-destroying explosion, usually after four seconds. Blocks destroyed by TNT always drop their usual items as if mined by a player.

It spawns mobs in waves, ejects consumable items and/or trial keys after they are all defeated, and then deactivates for 30 minutes. Having more Survival/Adventure mode players nearby results in more mobs and more rewards. A trial spawner will convert into an active ominous trial spawner during an ominous trial, even if it was on cooldo

lead: An ominous trial spawner is a trial spawner that has been altered by a Trial Omen effect carried by a player as part of an ominous trial. It spawns more dangerous mob waves, as well as ominous item spawners, but ejects better rewards and is the only source of ominous trial keys.

A vault is a block found in trial chambers that ejects loot when unlocked using a trial key. Each vault can be opened by an unlimited number of players, but each player can unlock a specific vault only once.
An ominous vault is a type of vault found in trial chambers. It ejects valuable loot when unlocked using an ominous trial key and is the only source of heavy cores, among other items.

A button is a non-solid block that produces a temporary redstone signal and powers its attached block when pressed by a player or a wind charge. The material a button is made of affects how long it remains pressed and whether it can be pressed by other means.
A wooden button is a type of button that remains pressed for longer than a stone button and can additionally be pressed by arrows and thrown tridents.
A stone button is a variant of the button, a non-solid block that produces a temporary redstone signal when pressed by a player or when hit by a wind charge.

A polished blackstone button is a variant of the button that shares many common properties with stone buttons. Like stone buttons, a polished blackstone button is a non-solid block that produces a temporary redstone signal when pressed.

lead: A copper bulb is a light-emitting block. It toggles on or off when it receives a redstone pulse, and does not need continuous power to emit light. Its light level depends on its state of oxidation. Waxed copper bulbs do not oxidize, but otherwise function identically.

A crafter is a low-capacity storage block that can use its contents to craft items when given a redstone signal, ejecting the results into the world or into a container it is facing. Its inventory slots can be individually locked so hoppers and similar blocks cannot fill them, while not affecting crafting recipes.

A daylight detector (also known as a daylight sensor) is a block that outputs a redstone signal based on its exposure to sky light. Using the detector inverts it, causing it instead to output a constant strong signal that weakens from exposure to sky light.

A dispenser is a low-capacity storage block that can fire projectiles, use certain items and tools, as well as place certain blocks, fluids, or entities when given a redstone signal. Items that do not have unique dispenser functions are instead ejected into the world like a dropper.
A dropper is a low-capacity storage block that can eject its contents into the world or into other containers when given a redstone signal.
A door is a block that serves as a switchable barrier to entity movement.
The copper door is a type of door made of copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.

The iron door is a variant of the door made of iron that can only be opened using redstone. Iron doors are more secure than wooden and copper doors because they cannot be opened by hand and cannot be broken by zombies. They are also more resistant to explosions, and immune to fire and lava.
A wooden door is a variant of the door that is made of wood and can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.

props.Transparent: JE: Partial (diffuses sky light) BE: Yes

lead: A honey block is a storage block equivalent to the contents of four honey bottles. It is sticky, can prevent jumping, and can be used in conjunction with pistons to move blocks and adhered entities.

props.Transparent: JE: YesBE: Partial (diffuses sky light, -2 to light)

lead: A hopper is a low-capacity storage block that can be used to collect item entities directly above it, as well as to transfer items into and out of other containers. A hopper can be locked with redstone power to stop it from moving items into or out of itself.
The lever is a non-solid block that can be switched to provide redstone power.

A lightning rod is a block that, with sky access, causes natural lightning strikes in a large area to only target itself. Getting struck by lightning causes it to emit a redstone signal and, if it is not waxed, also reduces its level of oxidation.

A note block is a block that emits sounds when attacked, used, or powered. The sound produced can be altered in various ways by using it or putting certain blocks directly above or below it. Allays are affected by note blocks, staying nearby and dropping held items next to it for a short while upon hearing its sound.
An observer is a block that emits a quick redstone pulse from its output side whenever its "face" detects that the block, fluid, or air directly in front of it has changed.

A piston is a block capable of pushing most entities and blocks when given a redstone signal. Some blocks cannot be moved, break when pushed or have other interactions with pistons. A piston can move up to twelve blocks at once.
A sticky piston is a variant of the piston that can additionally pull most blocks when it retracts.
A pressure plate is a non-solid block that produces a redstone signal when stood on by an entity, with multiple variants that have different properties.
A wooden pressure plate is a wooden variant of the pressure plate. It can detect all entities, producing the maximum signal strength of 15. Wooden pressure plates come in all variants of wood.
A stone pressure plate is a stone variant of the pressure plate that can detect only players and mobs.
A polished blackstone pressure plate is a polished blackstone variant of the pressure plate that can detect only players and mobs.

A heavy weighted pressure plate is a type of pressure plate that produces a redstone signal while one or more entities stand on it. Depending on how many entities are detected, the outputted signal strength will range from 1 to 15.

A light weighted pressure plate is a type of pressure plate that produces a redstone signal while one or more entities stand on it. Depending on how many entities are detected, the outputted signal strength will range from 1 to 15.

A rail is a non-solid block that provides a path along which minecarts can travel, and can be placed either flat on the ground, as a ramp, or curved. A curved rail allows minecarts to turn corners, and can rotate to connect to a different rail line while powered.

An activator rail is a type of rail that, if powered, can eject entities from regular minecarts, lock hopper minecarts, ignite TNT minecarts, and activate the command in a command block minecart. If not powered, it can only unlock locked hopper minecarts.
The detector rail is a type of rail that produces a redstone signal while a minecart is on it.

A powered rail is a type of rail that either increases or halts the velocity of minecarts depending on its power state, and can be used to accelerate a minecart from a standstill when placed facing a conductive block.
A redstone lamp is a solid block that produces light while it is receiving redstone power.

Redstone dust (often just called redstone) is a mineral used in crafting, brewing, and trimming, as well as being used as a placeable wire. Redstone wire is a non-solid block that can transmit a redstone power signal up to 15 blocks in distance; signal strengths below 15 have reduced distance. Redstone wire can power blocks it is placed on or pointing at.

A redstone comparator‌[JE only] or comparator‌[BE only] is a block that can compare the strength of two different redstone signals or subtract one from the other. It can also read the fullness of containers and the state of a few selected blocks.

A redstone repeater is a block that produces a full-strength redstone signal from its front while its back is powered, with four toggleable delay settings. It can also be locked into its current power state by directly powering its side with another repeater or a redstone comparator.

A redstone torch is a non-solid block that produces a full-strength redstone signal on all sides adjacent to it, except for its attached block, and can power the block directly above it. It deactivates while the block it is attached to is powered.

A slime block is a storage block equivalent to nine slimeballs. It has sticky and bouncy properties, making it useful in conjunction with pistons to move both blocks and entities. It can be used to brew potions of Oozing.
A target is a block that produces a temporary redstone signal when hit by a projectile. Unlike most other conductive blocks, it also redirects adjacent redstone dust toward it.

A trapped chest is a type of chest that functions identically to its base counterpart, but has a red-tinted latch and produces redstone power while open. Like normal chests, two trapped chests can merge into a large trapped chest if placed next to each other.
A trapdoor is a solid block that can be used as an openable 1×1 block barrier.

A copper trapdoor is a type of trapdoor made from copper that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone. A copper trapdoor can exist in one of eight variants depending on how oxidized it is and whether it is waxed or not.
An iron trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be only opened using redstone mechanisms.
A wooden trapdoor is a variant of the trapdoor that can be opened and closed by the player without redstone.
A fence gate is a block that shares the functions of both the door and the fence.

A tripwire hook is a block used to create a tripwire circuit, which requires two hooks and a straight horizontal line of 1-40 string. Both hooks in a valid circuit emit a redstone signal and power their attached blocks while any of the string is being touched by an entity, or if any string is broken without using shears.
String is an item that can be used as a crafting material or placed as a tripwire to allow tripwire hooks and observers to detect entities that touch it.
Allow is a block that can be used to create areas where players can build in spite of restrictions that would otherwise prevent them from doing so.
Border blocks are unbreakable blocks that prohibit any movement through, over or under them.
A chalkboard is a block that can display more text than a sign. Three sizes are available: 1×1 (slate), 2×1 (poster), and 3×2 (board).
The compound creator is a block used in chemistry. It allows over 30 compounds to be created by combining elements. This includes certain items which are available in the game normally.
Deny is a block that can be used to create areas where players cannot build.
The element constructor is a block used in chemistry. It allows the construction of elements by adjusting the number of protons, electrons, and neutrons.
Heat block is a block that can melt snow and ice like a torch, but it does not give off light.

props.Drops: Item Frame (1) The item it contains.

lead: An item frame is an entity‌[JE only] or block‌[BE only] that displays the item or block that is inside of it.

props.Drops: Glow Item Frame (1) The item it contains.

lead: A glow item frame is an entity‌[JE only] or block‌[BE only] that keeps itself and the item inside of it illuminated, even in the dark.
The lab table is a chemistry table used to make items and blocks from compounds (there are currently only five).
The material reducer is a block used in chemistry to learn about the natural world, by reducing Minecraft blocks to the elements that they contain.
Underwater TNT is a block that can be used by the player to initiate a controlled explosion underwater.
The underwater torch is a non-solid block that emits light underwater.
A barrier is an invisible block used to create solid boundaries.

A command block is an indestructible block that can execute commands. Jigsaw blocks are technical blocks commonly used as a way to construct large structures from smaller sections.
Lights are invisible blocks, primarily intended for map makers, that can produce any light level from 0 to 15.

lead: A petrified oak slab, known generically as a wooden slab in Bedrock Edition, is a unique type of slab available through commands or by upgrading from legacy versions. Unlike all other slabs, they are unobtainable in vanilla Survival gameplay.
The player head is a block based on the head of a player's skin (Steve by default). Player heads cannot be obtained in Survival.
A structure block is used to generate structures manually. They can also be used to save and load structures, alongside structure void blocks.
A structure void is an invisible block that is not saved by structure blocks, allowing for the creation of structures that leave some existing blocks unchanged when loaded in a different location.
A test block is a technical block that is used for game tests.
A test instance block is a technical block that is used for game tests.

tile.micro_block.name is an item used to shrink the shape of blocks in specific areas of the game into smaller individual blocks for display purposes. Currently, only pre-micro blocks are available in the game. Pre-micro blocks are generated using the modsdk interface, which creates the corresponding micro block data.
